subject: kingsnake
title: This Snake Eats Rattlesnakes, and Their Venom Doesn't Work on It

scenes.text: Rattlesnakes have one predator that bites them back. It isn't bigger. It isn't venomous.
The kingsnake. Up to six feet long, and about a quarter of its diet is other snakes, including rattlesnakes and copperheads.
Viper venom barely affects it. So it bites the head, wraps around, and squeezes.
Scientists measured that squeeze on almost 200 snakes. Kingsnakes pressed about twice as hard as rat snakes of the same size. Harder than a human heart pumps.
The secret isn't muscle. Both have the same amount. Kingsnakes coil in a neat spring, like a curly fry. Rat snakes make a loose pile.
It can swallow a snake over a third longer than itself. The rattle goes in last.

description:
Kingsnakes eat other snakes, including rattlesnakes, because viper venom has little effect on them and because they squeeze harder than any snake their size.
In a 2017 study of almost 200 snakes, kingsnakes constricted with about twice the pressure of rat snakes, around 20 kilopascals, more than a human heart. They have no extra muscle; they coil in tight, even spirals while rat snakes coil in a loose heap. A kingsnake can swallow a snake up to 35 percent longer than itself.
Which snake would you bet on in a fight? Comment below.
